title: Standing Sound Waves in Pipes
short: Open pipes resonate at fₙ = nv/(2L); pipes closed at one end only at odd multiples of v/(4L).
trouble: Students give a pipe closed at one end the same set of harmonics as an open pipe.

blocks.html: Flutes, organ pipes and clarinets make music with standing sound waves in air columns. The idea is the same as for strings, but the ends work differently. As in Sound: Pitch and Loudness, sound is air moving back and forth along the pipe.

Open at both ends (all harmonics): $$f_n = \frac{nv}{2L}, \quad n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$$ Closed at one end (odd harmonics only): $$f_n = \frac{nv}{4L}, \quad n = 1, 3, 5, \dots$$ A closed end is a displacement node; an open end is a displacement antinode.

blocks.name: ph-wave

opts.task: Switch between an open and a closed pipe and compare which harmonics are allowed.

blocks.cap: A pipe closed at one end in its third harmonic: a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end.

blocks.html: Air can't move through a closed end, so it is a node. At an open end the air moves freely, so it is an antinode. Open–open: antinode to antinode, a whole number of half wavelengths, just like a string. Closed–open: node to antinode, an odd number of quarter wavelengths, $L = n\frac{\lambda}{4}$ with $n$ odd. The even ones would need a node at the open end, which can't happen.

Giving a pipe closed at one end the same harmonics as an open pipe. A closed pipe has only odd multiples of its fundamental, and its fundamental is half that of an open pipe of the same length. Check: closed-pipe frequencies like $150, 250, 350\ \text{Hz}$ step by $2f_1$, and $f_1 = 50\ \text{Hz}$ itself is half the step.

blocks.title: Open and closed
blocks.q: Find the first two resonant frequencies of a $0.50\ \text{m}$ pipe ($v = 343\ \text{m/s}$), first open at both ends, then closed at one end.

blocks.title: Which kind of pipe?
blocks.q: A pipe resonates at $150$, $250$ and $350\ \text{Hz}$, and at no frequencies between them. Is it open or closed at one end? How long is it? ($v = 343\ \text{m/s}$.)
steps: Neighbors differ by $100\ \text{Hz}$. If it were open, the frequencies would be multiples of $100$, but $150$ is not.
They are $3, 5, 7$ times $50\ \text{Hz}$: odd multiples, so the pipe is closed at one end with $f_1 = 50\ \text{Hz}$.
blocks.a: Closed at one end, about $1.7\ \text{m}$ long
